New machine. Its objects are: temulor, fudoti, lamesen, pidofik, maleres, timinir.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: temulor, fudoti, lamesen
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test lit up, but I don't yet know the rule: the machine might light when any nexiom is present, only when both are, or only when exactly one is. Testing the other three objects will help tell these rules apart and show where the nexioms are.

TEST: pidofik, maleres, timinir
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Since the first group lit up and the second did not, both nexioms must be among temulor, fudoti and lamesen:
- **Any nexiom present lights it:** both nexioms must be in the first group, since the second group had none.
- **Both nexioms needed to light it:** both must be in the first group.
- **Exactly one nexiom lights it:** the first group would hold one and the second group the other, so the second group should also have lit up. It didn't, so this rule is out.

That leaves three possible pairs: temulor+fudoti, temulor+lamesen, or fudoti+lamesen. The rule is still either "any nexiom" or "both needed".

Testing temulor alone is my next move:
- **If it lights:** the rule is "any nexiom" and temulor is a nexiom. Testing fudoti alone would then settle the pair.
- **If it doesn't:** several cases remain, so I may not be able to settle the answer with one test.

Two tests cannot cover every case, so this is a best effort rather than a guaranteed solution.

TEST: temulor
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Temulor alone did not light up, so I need to account for each rule that is still possible.

- **"Any nexiom lights it":** temulor is not a nexiom, so the pair must be fudoti + lamesen.
- **"Both needed to light it":** a single object can never light the machine, so all three pairs are still possible. These are temulor + fudoti, temulor + lamesen and fudoti + lamesen.

My last test is fudoti and lamesen together.
- **If it lights up:** the pair must be fudoti + lamesen under either rule.
- **If it doesn't:** the rule is "both needed" and the pair is temulor + fudoti or temulor + lamesen. I would have to guess between those two.

No single test can separate all the remaining cases, so this is the best option rather than a guaranteed answer.

TEST: fudoti, lamesen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Fudoti and lamesen together did not light up, which settles the rule but not the pair.

- **"Any nexiom lights it":** after temulor failed alone, this rule required the pair fudoti + lamesen. That pair would have lit up, so this rule is out.
- **"Both needed to light it":** this fits every result. Neither group of three lights the machine unless it holds both nexioms, and no single object or wrong pair can light it.

So the rule is "both needed". The first test showed both nexioms are among temulor, fudoti and lamesen, and the last test rules out fudoti + lamesen. Temulor must be one nexiom, and the other is either fudoti or lamesen.

No test separated those two, so this answer is a 50/50 guess between temulor + fudoti and temulor + lamesen.

ANSWER: nexioms = temulor, fudoti
One last question. If only fudoti were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up, though this rests on my inferred rule rather than a direct test.

The results only fit the rule that the machine lights up when both nexioms are on it together.
- **"Any nexiom lights it":** temulor alone failed, so the pair would have to be fudoti + lamesen. That pair together also failed, so this rule is out.
- **"Exactly one nexiom lights it":** this was already ruled out because the second group of three did not light up.

Under "both needed", a single object can never light the machine, whether or not fudoti is a nexiom. Fudoti alone would stay dark.

PROBE: no

The first test didn't light up. If the machine lights whenever any nexiom is present, both nexioms must be among biragus, rapapik and bezusin. I'll test one of those alone. If biragus lights, I'll test rapapik next. If it doesn't, the answer would be rapapik and bezusin. This plan relies on that guess about how the machine responds, which I haven't confirmed yet.

TEST: biragus
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Biragus alone didn't light. If any single nexiom lights the machine, the nexioms must be rapapik and bezusin. But I haven't confirmed the rule: the machine might need both nexioms together, in which case neither negative result rules much out. Testing rapapik and bezusin together checks both cases. If it lights, that pair is the answer whichever rule applies. If it doesn't light, the "any nexiom lights it" idea is wrong and I'll use my last test to sort out the rule.

TEST: rapapik, bezusin
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Three tests have all failed to light, including rapapik and bezusin together, so the "any single nexiom lights it" rule must be wrong. Two other rules still fit:

- **Lights only with exactly one nexiom present:** the nexioms would be two of gunasi, mufito and fedago, or else rapapik and bezusin.
- **Lights only when both nexioms are present:** many pairs are still possible.

One test can't separate all of these, so I'll pick one that narrows the first rule as much as possible. Under that rule, testing gunasi and rapapik together lights for gunasi+mufito, gunasi+fedago or rapapik+bezusin. It stays dark only for mufito+fedago. If it doesn't light, I'll answer mufito and fedago.

TEST: gunasi, rapapik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

All four tests stayed dark, and no single rule pins down the answer with certainty.

- **"Lights with exactly one nexiom present":** the last test leaves only mufito and fedago. Gunasi+mufito, gunasi+fedago and rapapik+bezusin would each have lit the gunasi+rapapik test.
- **"Lights only when both nexioms are present":** mufito and fedago would be ruled out, because they were together in the first test. Many other pairs, such as biragus with any other object, would still be possible. No single pair is favoured under this rule.

I'm going with the only rule that names one specific pair. This is a judgement call. If the "both needed" rule is the true one, this answer is wrong.

ANSWER: nexioms = mufito, fedago
One last question. If only fedago were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

I never tested fedago on its own, so this is a prediction from my assumed rule, not an observation.

My answer of mufito and fedago depends on the rule "the machine lights when exactly one nexiom is present." Under that rule, fedago alone is one nexiom by itself, so the machine would light. This also fits the first test: gunasi, mufito and fedago together contained two nexioms, which is why it stayed dark.

If the true rule were "lights only when both nexioms are present," fedago alone would not light. But under that rule my answer would also be wrong, since mufito and fedago were together in the dark first test. I'm staying consistent with the rule behind my answer, but I'm not confident.

PROBE: yes

You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

The machine's rule is unknown, so I'll start with a simple split. I'm testing half the objects to see whether a group containing possible nexioms lights it up.

TEST: lemire, davota, vuregor
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Under an "any nexiom lights it" rule, both nexioms would have to be among the other three objects. Testing that group next should help tell the possible rules apart.

TEST: zureki, pakedol, rukanes
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit up, so a single nexiom isn't enough to light the machine. The likeliest rule is that both nexioms must be present together, which means one is in {lemire, davota, vuregor} and the other is in {zureki, pakedol, rukanes}. That leaves 9 possible pairs, and 2 yes/no tests can't separate all of them, so I'll narrow it down as far as I can. This test lights up only if the pair is lemire or davota together with zureki or pakedol.

TEST: lemire, davota, zureki, pakedol
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Since neither half lit up on its own, the most likely rule is still that both nexioms must be on the machine together. The last test rules out lemire or davota paired with zureki or pakedol. That leaves 5 possible pairs: vuregor–zureki, vuregor–pakedol, vuregor–rukanes, lemire–rukanes and davota–rukanes. One yes/no test can't separate 5 options, so I'll split them as evenly as possible. This test lights up only for vuregor–rukanes or lemire–rukanes.

TEST: vuregor, rukanes, lemire
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Out of tests, so this is a guess between several possibilities I could not separate.

- **Rule:** Neither half lit up, so one nexiom alone is not enough. That makes "both nexioms must be present" the most likely rule. Under it, one nexiom is in {lemire, davota, vuregor} and the other is in {zureki, pakedol, rukanes}.
- **Test 3 (dark):** This rules out lemire or davota paired with zureki or pakedol.
- **Test 4 (dark):** This rules out vuregor–rukanes and lemire–rukanes.
- **Left under that rule:** vuregor–zureki, vuregor–pakedol and davota–rukanes. All three fit every result equally well.
- **Other rules:** I haven't proven the rule. If the machine instead lit up only when exactly one nexiom is present, the results would fit only zureki–pakedol. My tests couldn't separate these rules either.

I'm choosing vuregor–zureki among the three equal options. This is roughly a one-in-three guess.

ANSWER: nexioms = vuregor, zureki
One last question. If only vuregor were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Almost certainly not.

- **Test 1:** vuregor was on the machine with lemire and davota, and it stayed dark.
- **If "both nexioms needed" is right:** no single object can ever light the machine.
- **If "exactly one nexiom" is right:** the only consistent pair is zureki–pakedol. Vuregor isn't a nexiom, so it couldn't light the machine.
- **The remaining exception:** vuregor would need to light the machine alone, with lemire or davota cancelling it in test 1. That would need an unusual "blocking" rule that nothing in my results suggests.

PROBE: no
